etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English donoure, donour; from Anglo-Norman donour, from Old French doneur (See French donneur).

quote.citation: 1838 (date written), L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter VIII, in Lady Anne Granard; or, Keeping up Appearances. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], published 1842, →OCLC, page 104:
quote.text: "You prefer, then, having the money to the ornaments which I had intended for you?"/"Oh! the hundred pounds, certainly," exclaimed Isabella, colouring a little at the idea of trespassing on the donor's generosity.

definitions.definition: An object, typically broken beyond repair, that is used for spare parts.

quote.citation: 2004, Aaron Bonk, Honda Engine Swaps‎[1], CarTech, →ISBN, page 41:
quote.text: You'll need to lengthen the plug for the fan switch and swap its connector for that of the donor.

definitions.definition: (chemistry) A group or molecule that donates either a radical, electrons or a moiety in a chemical reaction. Compare acceptor.
